solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Be savage and be issued prison having broken a rule abroad

indicators.note: a prison that is broken is smashed apart, so its letters are scattered among the others
abroad here means spread widely about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: to go forth is to be sent out or issued
jug is slang for prison
taken as written

explanation.surface: A convict sent to a foreign jail after breaking the local law turns vicious.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison and the rule are mixed together, and the result follows the phrase for being issued.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for the jugular is an idiom for attacking ferociously at the weakest point, which is acting savagely.

clue.text: Cut flowers placed outside northern sex shop

indicators.note: something cut has had its end chopped off, so the flowers lose their final letter
in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the word is turned round
one thing placed outside another wraps around it, so the flowers enclose the other piece

blocks.note: a bouquet is a bunch of flowers
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A florist arranges cut flowers outside a sex shop in the north of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a coy euphemism for sex, and 'northern' only works because this is a down entry read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small, often fashionable, retail shop.

clue.text: Food regrettably thrown up, note

indicators.note: in a down clue throwing a word up makes it read from bottom to top, so it is backwards

blocks.note: alas expresses regret
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone sick after a meal, with a little note added about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food regrettably thrown up' suggests vomiting, but 'thrown up' only turns the word for regret upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a spicy cured sausage, an example of food.

clue.text: Guarantees pains will be treated for some senior citizens

indicators.note: things that are treated are processed and altered, so the letters will be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A promise that elderly people's aches will get medical treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Septuagenarians are people in their seventies, so they make up some of the elderly population.

clue.text: Lock-keeper's dilemma — only half of boat on river

blocks.note: to be in a fix is to be in a dilemma
the second half of the four-letter word boat
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A canal lock-keeper is in a quandary with just half a boat on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Lock-keeper looks like a canal official, but the locks are of hair: a fixature is a gel or pomade that keeps hair in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixature is a hair-fixing preparation, so it keeps locks of hair in place: a playful paraphrase.

clue.text: Journalist travelled up from the south to cover case of ill-treatment

indicators.note: going up from the bottom of a down entry means the word is read in the opposite direction
the case of something is its outer shell, so only the outermost letters are kept
to cover something is to go around it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: rode is a past tense meaning travelled
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A reporter travels north to cover a story about abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior journalist who prepares and commissions copy.

clue.text: Conventional sorts failed to be prestigious

indicators.note: something that has failed has broken down, so the letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Conformists who never managed to become distinguished.
explanation.definitionFit: The petits bourgeois are the lower middle class, stereotyped as conservative and conformist in outlook.

clue.text: Week off in two years at old western car manufacturer

indicators.note: the week is taken off from inside the next word, so that letter is removed
heading west in an across entry means reading from right to left

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for week
taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone takes a week off during two years at an old Western car maker.
explanation.walkthrough: TWO loses its W; then 'at old' together is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Toyota is a Japanese company that builds cars.

clue.text: Be withdrawn by party on backing wrong'un

indicators.note: something withdrawn is drawn back, so the word runs backwards
backing means going in reverse, so this word is read the other way

blocks.note: to be is to exist, or live
a do is a party
re means on, as in concerning

explanation.surface: A shy person at a party is supporting a bad lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong'un is a criminal or bad person, which is what an evildoer is.

clue.text: Picture feature on Left snubbed

indicators.note: snubbed suggests snubbing short, a stub, so the word loses its tip
in an across clue, one piece on another is written after it, so the feature goes second

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
a trait is a distinguishing feature

explanation.surface: A newspaper picture feature about the political Left being ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: Left is the nautical side of a ship, and snubbed means docked at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painted or photographed picture of a person.

clue.text: Edge past soldier, perhaps, in county

indicators.note: past means beyond, so this piece comes after the other in the reading order

blocks.note: a soldier is a kind of ant, hence 'perhaps'
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A soldier somewhere in the country edges past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier, perhaps' signals an example: soldier ants are a caste of ant. Antrim is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Cocktail time — anise liqueurs shaken

indicators.note: drinks that are shaken get mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cocktail hour, with aniseed liqueurs shaken in the cocktail shaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila sunrise is a cocktail of tequila, orange juice and grenadine.

clue.text: House alterations typically result herefrom

blocks.note: surface reading: building work on a home, such as an extension
setter's reading: the House is the House of Commons, whose membership changes after a nationwide vote

explanation.surface: Where home renovations usually come from.
explanation.walkthrough: House sounds like a dwelling, but it is the House of Commons, the elected chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A nationwide vote for Parliament is what changes the make-up of the House of Commons.

clue.text: General in Indian city securing international pass

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so the city wraps around the rest

blocks.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal
I is the abbreviation for international
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A general stationed in an Indian city securing an international route.
explanation.definitionFit: Agricola was the Roman general who governed Britain and was celebrated by his son-in-law Tacitus.

clue.text: Musical trio has Fourteenth Street essentially gushing about welcoming final character

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters of each word are kept
welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece goes inside another
about can mean turned around, so this word is read backwards

blocks.note: the two central letters of this ten-letter word
the two central letters of this six-letter word
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
OTT, over the top, describes gushing excess

explanation.surface: A trio playing on Fourteenth Street gushes about the last person to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' covers both Fourteenth and Street. Z goes inside the middle of Street, and over-the-top is read backwards at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A terzetto is an Italian term for a vocal or instrumental trio, or a piece for three performers.

clue.text: Rather urgent struggles involving male who eschews cultivated elements of consumerism?

definitions.text: who eschews cultivated elements of consumerism
definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a person

indicators.note: letters that struggle thrash about and end up in a new order
to involve is to take in, so the man is included among the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: Urgent battles over a man who rejects the trappings of a consumer society.
explanation.walkthrough: The male is added to the mixed letters before shuffling. Cultivated is a pun: farmed crops, not refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunter-gatherers live by foraging and hunting rather than farming, so they shun cultivated food.

clue.text: Did gas leak out in study periodically

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept
out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged
in puts one piece inside another

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gas leak happened in the study now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas is a verb here: to gas is to chatter, so 'Did gas' is the past tense of chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is informal for chatting at length, so having gassed is having talked.

clue.text: Bowler that's taken off could rest here

definitions.text: Bowler that's taken off could rest here

blocks.note: surface reading: a cricket bowler replaced by the captain, who goes off to rest

blocks.clueFragment: Bowler that's taken off could rest here
blocks.note: setter's reading: a bowler hat removed from the head is stored in a container

explanation.surface: Where a tired cricket bowler, withdrawn from the attack, might take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler is taken off when the captain stops him bowling; here the bowler is a hard round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A box designed for storing a hat, such as a bowler, when it is not being worn.

clue.text: Open bar, smooth on the inside?

indicators.note: only what lies on the inside is wanted, so the outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: a pub is a bar
slick means smooth

explanation.surface: A bar that is open, with a sleek interior.
explanation.definitionFit: Public means open to all, as in a public meeting.

clue.text: Drunken teens regularly tried last of scotch on the rocks

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
the last of a word is its final letter alone
drunken suggests staggering about, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
taken as written
the final letter

explanation.surface: Drunken teenagers kept trying the last of the whisky over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' looks like whisky with ice, but it means in financial trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the red means overdrawn or in debt, and a business on the rocks is failing financially.

clue.text: Indonesian ensemble adopts quiet strategy

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the ensemble takes another letter inside it

blocks.note: a gamelan is a traditional Indonesian percussion orchestra
p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: An Indonesian orchestra decides to play softly as a tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: A game plan is a planned strategy for achieving an aim.

clue.text: Surpass numpty following Open University

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: OU is the abbreviation for the Open University
a numpty and a twit are both fools

explanation.surface: A fool coming after a distance-learning university student does better.
explanation.walkthrough: Numpty is Scottish slang for an idiot. The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit is to get the better of someone by cleverness, so to surpass them.
